title: Animal and plant cells in different solutions
caption: Water always moves from the higher to the lower water potential. In pure water a red blood cell bursts but a plant cell only becomes turgid, because its wall pushes back. In a strong solution both lose water: the red cell crenates and the plant cell's membrane pulls away from its wall.
alt: Six panels: a red blood cell and a plant cell, each in a solution of higher, equal and lower water potential, with arrows showing water moving in, not moving, or moving out.
description: Red blood cell, ψ = −750 kPa. In pure water (ψ = 0) water enters and the cell bursts (haemolysis).
In a solution of ψ = −750 kPa there is no net movement.
In a solution of ψ = −1500 kPa water leaves and the cell shrinks and crenates.
Plant cell, ψ = ψs + ψp = −700 + 300 = −400 kPa. In pure water, water enters and the cell becomes fully turgid.
In a solution of ψ = −400 kPa there is no net movement.
In a solution of ψ = −1400 kPa, below the cell's solute potential, water leaves until the membrane pulls away from the wall: plasmolysis.
